mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to turn negative due to tightened credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in a single month
failure_condition: In a tightening regime, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) or the change in FEDFUNDS is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 0.2% is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as higher expected labor costs pressure corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or UNRATE change is not above 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDP demand (GDPC1) grows faster than supply (INDPRO), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is positive as market anticipates stronger economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > INDPRO growth rate in the same month
failure_condition: In >70% of such events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) or the signal is spurious (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 2% predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as it signals weak manufacturing demand.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or INDPRO recovers within the same month.

mechanism_narrative: During a period of falling CPIAUCSL inflation (monthly decline >0.3%), the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns positive as investors anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >0.3% in a month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or inflation does not fall as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: When employment (PAYEMS) rises by more than 50,000 jobs in a month, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is positive reflecting optimism about labor market strength.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50,000 in a month
failure_condition: Over 60 days, returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or job growth is not as forecasted.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in both demand (HOUST) and financial conditions (FEDFUNDS) above historical averages for two consecutive months create a positive 20-day forward return as market expects sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and FEDFUNDS increases in two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-side shock where industrial production (INDPRO) falls for three consecutive months predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate production constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or INDPRO recovers before the 60-day window.
